title: Unfractionated heparin (UFH)
keyNumbers: Protamine: 1 mg per 100 U UFH given in the prior 2–3 h, max 50 mg
Received heparin with aPTT >40 s: do not give IVT (AHA 2026 §4.6.5 Table 8: absolute contraindication; expert opinion, not graded)
UFH — therapeutic IV infusion: Label: 5,000 U IV bolus, then 20,000–40,000 U/24 h (68-kg basis); weight-based nomogram per local protocol
UFH — VTE prophylaxis: 5,000 U SC every 8–12 h
Label target: aPTT 1.5–2× control; check ~every 4 h early in infusion (label)
mechanism: Potentiates antithrombin → inactivates thrombin and factor Xa

uses.doseText: Label: 5,000 U IV bolus, then 20,000–40,000 U/24 h (68-kg basis); weight-based nomogram per local protocol
notes: Stroke/ICH-adjacent use: many centers omit the bolus — follow local neuro nomogram
Short half-life and full protamine reversal make it the choice when procedures or bleeding risk are likely
Label regimen is postoperative (5,000 U 2 h before surgery then q8–12h); same dose used for medical/stroke prophylaxis

renalHepatic: No renal adjustment — preferred over LMWH when CrCl <30 or dialysis is likely

holdBeforeProcedure: IV infusion: stop and confirm normalized aPTT before LP/procedure — interval per local policy
thrombolysisRule: Received heparin with aPTT >40 s: do not give IVT (AHA 2026 §4.6.5 Table 8: absolute contraindication; expert opinion, not graded)
Recent heparin: wait for aPTT before IVT — starting before coagulation results applies only without recent heparin or warfarin (AHA 2026 §4.6.5 Table 8; §4.6.1 Rec 10: COR 2a, B-NR)

reversal.doseText: 1 mg per 100 U UFH given in the prior 2–3 h, max 50 mg (unstructured: see protamine)

monitoring: Label target: aPTT 1.5–2× control; check ~every 4 h early in infusion (label)
Anti-Xa targets and nomograms are institutional
Platelets periodically for HIT; platelets usually fall 5–10 days after starting; rapid-onset HIT within 24 h if heparin in the prior 3 months (label)
interactions: Hyperkalemia: check K+ before and during therapy in at-risk patients (label)
pregnancy: Safe in pregnancy and does not pass into breast milk (Miller 2026)
institutionVaries: Weight-based nomogram (bolus/no bolus, starting rate, aPTT vs anti-Xa target) — use the local stroke/neuro nomogram
LP/neuraxial holds: see periprocedural-holds-lp-evd (ASRA 2025); label intervals are for surgery
pearls: Contraindicated: history of HIT/HITT, pork/heparin hypersensitivity, or when coagulation tests can't be done for full-dose use (label)
Suspected HIT: stop all heparin, including flushes
